title: Five-point report errors permit negative heat slopes in three of four Atlantic and Pacific coral samples in 2003-2019
abstract: We tested bounded errors in reported coral bleaching in 9,623 Reef Check surveys. Four Atlantic and Pacific models for 2003-2019 controlled country, year, month and depth. If each report can differ from its true value by at most five percentage points, exact bounds permit a negative heat slope in three samples. The early Atlantic slope stays positive. The smallest all-report error limits that reach zero are 7.862, 2.050, 3.301 and 3.722 points. With zero reports exact, five-point errors permit a negative slope only in the later Atlantic sample. If only positive multiples of five can vary by 2.5 points, all four slopes stay positive. These are fixed-record sensitivity bounds, not evidence that errors occurred. Three baseline sampling intervals already include zero. Selected visits, missing outcomes, site confounding, surface exposure and permissive error alignment limit inference. The package includes source hashes, survey records, attainable outcome assignments, code, independent checks and a figure.

display.caption: Exact lower heat-slope bounds as the maximum report error increases. Three masks separate changes to all reports, positive reports, and positive multiples of five. Errors can align with heat. These are fixed-file bounds, not confidence intervals.
